title: Canonical ordinary/completed tensor comparison is Frobenius-equivariant
statement:
Fix $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ of characteristic $p$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with ring of integers $R$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme $W_0$ with geometric fibre $W$. For integral bounded-constructible objects $M,N\in D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)$ in the coefficient conventions of [def-wf-weil-category], let $B=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$, let $T=M\otimes^L_BN$, and let $\widehat T=M\widehat\otimes^L_RN$ be the completed tensor of [def-wf-tensor-product]. The canonical comparison $\chi:T\xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat T$ of [lem-fix-constructible-tensor-completion], followed by the intrinsic completion identification of [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion], is natural in $M,N$. If $M,N$ carry Weil maps and $\Phi_W$ is geometric Frobenius, let $\varphi_T=(\varphi_M\otimes^L\varphi_N)\circ\mu^{\mathrm{ord}}_{\Phi_W}$ and $\varphi_{\widehat T}=(\varphi_M\otimes^L\varphi_N)\circ\widehat\mu_{\Phi_W}$ be the tensor Weil maps defined using the two canonical pullback-tensor comparisons. Then
$$\chi\circ\varphi_T=\varphi_{\widehat T}\circ\Phi_W^*(\chi).$$
Thus the induced isomorphism between $T$ and $\widehat T$ is a morphism in the Weil category, and the assertion remains valid after rationalization and passage to a common finite coefficient field.
